subject: Discrepancy between glm and stan_glm for the Gamma family

messages.author: c1ef9a97cbbb91f5
messages.subject: Discrepancy between glm and stan_glm for the Gamma family
parts:
I ran the following Gamma regression with an identity link. The results from glm and stan_glm are very different. Any ideas why this is happening? Thanks. 


library(rstanarm)
clotting <- data.frame(
  u = c(5,10,15,20,30,40,60,80,100),
  lot1 = c(118,58,42,35,27,25,21,19,18),
  lot2 = c(69,35,26,21,18,16,13,12,12))

f <- glm(lot1 ~ log(u), data = clotting, family = Gamma(link = "identity"))
g <- stan_glm(lot1 ~ log(u), data = clotting, family = Gamma(link = "identity"))
coef(f)
coef(g)


> coef(f)
(Intercept)      log(u) 
   99.25045   -18.37432 
> coef(g)
(Intercept)      log(u) 
  33.389419   -1.274331

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: Discrepancy between glm and stan_glm for the Gamma family
parts:
There are at least three factors that are combining to produce this discrepancy: 

(1) There aren't very many observations
(2) The parameters are pretty large
(3) The identity link

What you're seeing is the combination of 1, 2, and 3 making the default rstanarm priors that are typically weakly informative actually quite strongly informative. This wouldn't be an issue with a log link (or if the data were rescaled) because that would make the parameter estimates much smaller. 

I bet if you set the prior and prior_intercept arguments to NULL (which removes the priors) or set the scale parameters of the normal priors for prior and prior_intercept to a large value then you'll see more similar results to glm. 

Hope that helps,

Jonah
